context: Treat each independently. For benchbox admin, decide whether Phase 3 is still planned; if so mark the runbook explicitly as not-yet-implemented, if not delete it. For the explorer ADR, at minimum correct the present-tense Context so an Accepted record stops describing deleted files as current. For TPC-DI, either build a configuration API matching the documented shape or delete the section and document the real enable_parallel/max_workers interface.
description: Surfaced 2026-08-17/18 by the documentation audit, which deliberately left these alone because each needs a build-or-delete decision rather than a doc edit. (1) benchbox admin: docs/operations/results-phase-3-runbook.md documents admin revoke-token, review, promote, reject, withdraw, verify-window, revoke-all-tokens, block-actor and withdraw-all across lines 47-396, plus benchbox result withdraw at :164, and docs/reference/threat-model.md:31 lists the surface in its Phase column. No admin command is registered on the CLI. (2) benchbox explorer build / build-contract: docs/development/adr/adr-explorer-cli-surface.md describes it across lines 13-218 and the ADR is marked Accepted, but no explorer command is registered - only an explorer extra in pyproject.toml:110. The ADR's Context section also describes benchbox/cli/commands/explorer.py and benchbox/core/explorer_pipeline/ in the present tense; both paths have since been deleted, so an Accepted ADR now makes false statements about the current tree. (3) TPC-DI parallel execution: docs/guides/tpc/tpc-di-deployment-guide.md builds six code blocks across lines 336-835 on ParallelBenchmarkConfig, ParallelExecutionMode and ParallelWorkloadType, none of which exist. The real API is TPCDIBenchmark(enable_parallel: bool, max_workers: int); ParallelProcessingConfig exists at benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/parallel_batch_processor.py:102 but is constructed internally and shares none of the documented fields. Each case teaches a reader a surface that will fail the moment they use it.
